author: agent
text:
DEFECT, measured 2026-08-16 during the 0.54.0 close: this is presented as a read (`memway --json verify-change`, one of the seven JSON queries) and it WRITES. Fingerprinting .coord around one call on a repo whose tree had moved ahead of its map: five files rewritten - index/coordinates.json, index/edges.json, index/parse_cache.json, cache/coordinates.pkl, cache/edges.pkl. summary and attention, measured the same way in the same run, wrote nothing.

It shipped in 0.52.1 as the seventh --json query and was never added to READS in tests/test_read_fence.py, whose table holds before_edit, show, summary, at, lineage, viz, dig - and whose own docstring says "Every read surface, same measurement. Do not exempt one." The fence did not fail because the surface was never enrolled; CLAUDE.md lesson 3 says a new read surface goes under read_only() AND into that test, and only half of that happened.

How it surfaced: .coord/index/* turned up modified in a working tree where I had run no index. I first attributed it to memway_meta via MCP, which was wrong - isolated measurement shows memway_meta writes exactly ONE file, the note itself. Attribution from `git status` after a compound command is not measurement.

Sharper after 0.54.0: a "read" that reindexes can now perform the sketch migration, and the migration announces itself on stdout, which a --json caller has no reason to display.

Fix is read_only() plus enrolment in READS; both, or the next one hides the same way.
